item.title: A Repeatable Microsoft 365 Offboarding Script with Graph PowerShell
item.description:
Overview

Offboarding is one of those tasks that’s simple on paper and easy to get subtly wrong in practice. Miss a step and you end up with a departed user who still has an active session token, a mailbox nobody can read, or a license you’re paying for months later.

Between employees and a steady rotation of contractors, I was offboarding people often enough that a checklist in my head wasn’t good enough. This post walks through the script I use now. It takes a UPN and runs the whole sequence the same way every time.

item.title: Replacing Excel with a SharePoint List for Inventory Management
item.description:
Introduction

Managing a small inventory in Excel can be convenient at first—but as the inventory grows, Excel often becomes more of a bottleneck than a solution. I recently decided to shift from an Excel-based approach to a SharePoint List for better flexibility, multi-user access, and integration potential with APIs (like Dell’s warranty service).

In this post, I’ll walk you through:

  1. Why I moved from Excel to SharePoint
  2. How I set up the SharePoint List
  3. Automating warranty checks with the Dell API
  4. Lessons learned and future ideas
